question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To get on one's nerves
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase which best expresses the meaning of the idiom* "To get on one's nerves"* is:* "To irritate or provoke one"*
 
• **"To get on one's nerves" **is an idiom that means to annoy, irritate, or bother someone.(चिढ़ना)
 
• If something or someone gets on your nerves, they annoy or irritate you.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is:** 'To irritate or provoke one'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Explanation of the other options:
 
 
• **"To unnecessary stretch the conversation"** means to extend the discussion or conversation unnecessarily. (बातचीत को अनावश्यक रूप से बढ़ाना)
 
• **"To become highly successful"** means to attain a high level of success or achievement. (बहुत अधिक सफल होना)
 
• **"To get in someone's mind" **means to become a prevalent thought or consideration in someone's mind. (किसी के मन में प्रवेश करना)
